title: Prop 2(i): 'not definable from 𝓕' inferred from absence of vocabulary (non-sequitur)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
Proposition 2(i) concludes non-definability of 𝓞_Φ from 𝓕 because (O1)–(O3) contain no behavioural predicate and 𝓕's definiens 'never occurs' in the definiens of 𝓞_Φ. But non-occurrence of vocabulary in one chosen formulation does NOT establish non-definability/non-reducibility: two predicates can be coextensive (hence inter-definable up to extension) though their canonical definitions share no vocabulary. The argument conflates *intensional distinctness of the stated definitions* with *definability/reducibility*.

Constraint (a) ('does not reduce to a sociological description') requires a precise notion of reduction (extensional coextension / supervenience / analytic equivalence) and a disproof of it. The cleanest fix: delete 2(i) and strengthen 2(ii) to non-coextension + non-supervenience — exhibit two scenarios identical in 𝓕 but differing in 𝓞_Φ, so 𝓞_Φ does not supervene on 𝓕.
